proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 e_{p,n}=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
For a random variable \(Z\in[0,1]\), let
\(\psi(\lambda)=\log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\).  Exponential tilting gives
\(\psi''(\lambda)=\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)\le 1/4\), since
\(\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)\le
E_{\lambda}[(Z-1/2)^2]\le1/4\).  Because
\(\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0\), two integrations yield
\[
 \log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\le\lambda^2/8,
 \qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes
\(\widehat p_x\) the average of \(n\) independent Bernoulli variables
with mean \(p_x\).  Exponential Markov's inequality, (1), and optimization
at \(\lambda=4e_{p,n}\) give
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \bigl(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>e_{p,n}\bigr)
 \le 2e^{-2ne_{p,n}^2}=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.                            \tag{2}
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le e_{p,n}\right)
 \ge1-\frac{\alpha}{3}.                                               \tag{3}
\]
The true mass vector is nonnegative and sums to one.  Thus the event in
(3) is exactly the event that this vector belongs to
\(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), by
\(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\); the asserted
coordinate bound follows from the same definition.

For the count assertion, if \(N\) is binomial with parameters \(n\) and
\(p\), then, for every \(t>0\), exponential Markov's inequality and
\(1-p+pe^{-t}\le\exp\{p(e^{-t}-1)\}\) imply
\[
 \Pr(N\le np/2)
 \le \exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\log2\) makes the exponent
\(-np(1-\log2)/2\le-np/8\).  Since \(n_x\) is binomial with parameters
\(n\) and \(p_x\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 &\le \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(n_x<np_x/2)\\
 &\le m e^{-np_{\min}/8}.                                             \tag{4}
 \end{split}
\]

It remains to quantify mass profiling for the relaxed outer sieve.  Let
\(p=(p_x)\) and \(p'=(p'_x)\) belong to
\(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and fix
\(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\).  Put
\(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  By
\(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\), for \(a\in I\),
\[
 f_x(a)\ge\kappa/2,
 \qquad
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)+e_n.
\]
Consequently, using the definition
\(b_{\mu,n}=4e_n/\kappa\),
\[
 \left|\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                               \tag{5}
\]
Both mass vectors are within \(e_{p,n}\) of \(\widehat p\) coordinatewise,
so (5) gives
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
 \right|
 \le 2m\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n}.                    \tag{6}
\]
Let \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>1\).  From
\(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}tuning\text{-}grid}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\),
\(K_n\sim\log n/\log\log n\) and
\(b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{-\gamma})=O(r_n)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \log\left(\frac{e_{p,n}}{r_n}\right)
 =-\frac12\log n+O(\log\log n)\longrightarrow-\infty.
\]
Thus the right side of (6) is \(o(r_n)\), completing all assertions of
the corrected lemma.

Fix a sufficiently large \(n\).  We first establish the simultaneous
confidence event.  Conditional on the labels \((X_i)_{i=1}^n\), the
observations in a nonempty cell are independent and have the conditional
law given \(X=x\), by \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\).  Each real and imaginary
part of a probability-channel summand belongs to \([-1,1]\).  Assumptions
\(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\),
\(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\) imply \(|Y|\le B_Y\) almost
surely, so each real and imaginary part of a marked-channel summand belongs
to \([-B_Y,B_Y]\).

Apply the moment-generating-function argument in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), after rescaling an interval of
length \(2c\), separately to the real and imaginary parts.  Since
\(|z|>u\) implies
\(\max\{|\operatorname{Re}z|,|\operatorname{Im}z|\}>u/\sqrt2\), when
\(n_x>\lambda_n\) this gives, for every \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\),
\[
 \Pr\left(
 |\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|
 >2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\ \middle|\ (X_i)_{i=1}^n
 \right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n},                                           \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \Pr\left(
 |\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-G_x(s,t)|
 >2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\ \middle|\ (X_i)_{i=1}^n
 \right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n}.                                           \tag{8}
\]
If \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), then the definitions of the empirical channels,
including the empty-cell convention, and the bounds
\(|F_x|\le1\), \(|G_x|\le B_Y\) show deterministically that the same
inequalities hold with the radii \(\rho^F_{x,n}=2\) and
\(\rho^G_{x,n}=2B_Y\).  Hence a conditional union bound over the two
channels, the cells, and the frequency grid gives failure probability at
most
\[
 8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6.                  \tag{9}
\]
Combining (9) with the mass-region failure probability \(\alpha/3\) from
\(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), then integrating over the
labels, yields
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 (\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})
 \ge1-\alpha/3-\alpha/6\ge1-\alpha.                                  \tag{10}
\]

Suppose now that \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) occurs.  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\) in each of the
finitely many cells and
\(\mathrm{lem{:}atomic\text{-}grid\text{-}embedding}\) to both errors.
Define the proof-intermediate tuple
\[
 \bar\theta_n=
 \bigl((p_x,\widetilde f_{x,n},\widetilde q_{x,n})_{x\in\mathcal X},
       \bar\phi_{1,n},\bar\phi_{2,n}\bigr).
\]
Its mass vector is in \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) by the event.  If
\((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\), then \(s,t\in\Gamma_n\).  Characteristic
functions have modulus at most one.  Also \(|\widehat f_x(u)|\le1\), and
\(|\widehat q_x(u)|\le\int|q_x|\le B_Y\), the latter because
\(q_x=m_xf_x\), \(f_x\) is a density, and \(|m_x|\le B_Y\).  The transform
of a uniform approximation on the interval of length \(2B_A\) differs by
at most \(2B_A\) times that approximation error.  Therefore the
factorization in \(\mathrm{lem{:}factorization}\), the two embedding
lemmas, and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\left|
 \widehat{\widetilde f}_{x,n}(s+t)
 \bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-F_x(s,t)
 \right|
 \le2B_Aa_{f,n}+2\tau_{e,n}\le\delta^F_n,\\
 &\left|
 \widehat{\widetilde q}_{x,n}(s+t)
 \bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-G_x(s,t)
 \right|
 \le2B_Aa_{q,n}+2B_Y\tau_{e,n}\le\delta^G_n.                         \tag{11}
 \end{split}
\]
For example, the error-product term in the first line is bounded by
\[
 |\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)|
 \le|\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)-\phi_1(s)|
   +|\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-\phi_2(t)|
 \le2\tau_{e,n},
\]
and the marked line is identical after multiplying this bound by \(B_Y\).
Combining (11) with the empirical inequalities in
\(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) proves every residual constraint in
\(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}feasible\text{-}set}\).  The embedding
lemmas give all deterministic sieve constraints.  Hence
\[
 \bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}.                                    \tag{12}
\]
The quotient conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\), applied with
the true mass vector, now gives
\[
 \|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}.             \tag{13}
\]

Finally, consider an arbitrary realized sample.  Put
\(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  For any
\(\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), the mass constraints, the relaxed marked
envelope, and \(f_x\ge\kappa/2\) on \(I\) yield
\[
 |\mu_\theta(a)|
 \le\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x
 \left(B_Y+\frac{e_n}{f_x(a)}\right)
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                               \tag{14}
\]
If the feasible set is nonempty, set
\(\ell(a)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)\) and
\(u(a)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)\).  Equation
(14) implies
\[
 \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le B_Y,
 \qquad
 -B_Y\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n},
 \qquad
 \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n}.                               \tag{15}
\]
Together with \(-B_Y\le B_Y\), these are precisely the four pairwise
inequalities needed to conclude
\[
 \max\{-B_Y,\ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\}
 \le
 \min\{B_Y,u(a)+b_{\mu,n}\}.
\]
Both endpoints lie in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\).  If the feasible set is empty,
both endpoints equal zero by
\(\mathrm{def{:}profiled\text{-}band}\).  Thus, for every sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad(a\in I),
 \qquad 0\le W_n\le2B_Y.                                              \tag{16}
\]
Equations (10), (12), (13), and (16) prove the lemma.

Fix \(n\) at least as large as the common deterministic threshold in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\).  We first
verify the measurability and finiteness asserted for the explicit
construction.  At this fixed \(n\), the deterministic signal families are
compact.  Indeed, their defining inequalities are closed; for
\(f\in\mathscr F_n\), the lower bound \(f\ge-a_{f,n}\) and the bounded
integral imply a uniform \(L^1(\mathcal A)\) bound, hence a coefficient
bound by equivalence of norms on the fixed finite-dimensional spline
space.  The envelope defining \(\mathscr Q_n(f)\) then gives the same
conclusion for \(q\).  The error families are closed subsets of the
product of a finite simplex and \([-H_n,H_n]^{M_n}\), and hence are
compact.  The mass simplex is compact as well.  Let \(K\) denote the
resulting fixed compact coefficient--weight--atom box after imposing all
deterministic constraints.

For a realized sample \(z\), let \(h(z,\theta)\) be the maximum of zero
and the positive parts of the finitely many mass-confidence and channel
residual violations in
\(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}feasible\text{-}set}\).  Then
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)=\{\theta\in K:h(z,\theta)=0\}.                   \tag{17}
\]
The map \(h\) is measurable in \(z\) and continuous in \(\theta\), since
the empirical transforms are measurable and every fitted transform is a
finite continuous function of its coefficients, weights, and atoms.
Because every feasible density is at least \(\kappa/2\) on \(I\), the map
\((a,\theta)\mapsto\mu_\theta(a)\) is continuous on \(I\times K\).

For completeness, these facts imply measurability of the profiled extrema
without an unproved selection assertion.  Let \(K_0\) be a countable dense
subset of \(K\), and define
\[
 d(z)=\inf_{\theta\in K}h(z,\theta),
 \qquad
 V_k^+(z,a)=\sup_{\theta\in K}
 \{\mu_\theta(a)-kh(z,\theta)\},
\]
with \(V_k^-\) defined by replacing \(\mu_\theta\) with
\(-\mu_\theta\).  Continuity in \(\theta\) permits every infimum and
supremum here to be taken over \(K_0\); hence \(d,V_k^+,V_k^-\) are jointly
measurable in their displayed arguments.  Compactness shows that
\(d(z)=0\) exactly when \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)\ne\varnothing\).  On this
event,
\[
 V_k^+(z,a)\downarrow
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a),
 \qquad
 V_k^-(z,a)\downarrow
 -\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a).                 \tag{18}
\]
To prove the first limit, choose maximizers in \(K\).  Any convergent
subsequence of maximizers must have \(h=0\), since a feasible point gives
a fixed finite lower bound whereas a point with violation bounded away
from zero incurs penalty tending to minus infinity.  Its limiting
objective is therefore no larger than the feasible supremum; the reverse
inequality holds because feasible points have zero penalty.  The second
limit is the same argument applied to \(-\mu_\theta\).
Thus (18), the measurable event \(\{d=0\}\), and the stipulated zero value
on \(\{d>0\}\) prove joint sample-and-index measurability of the extrema.
Maxima and minima with the constants \(\pm B_Y\) preserve measurability.
Equation (14) of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) proves their
finiteness, while its equation (16) proves, for every sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad(a\in I),
 \qquad 0\le W_n\le2B_Y.                                              \tag{19}
\]

Let \(P\in\mathcal M\).  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the same lemma
provides \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) with
\(|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-\mu(a)|\le b_{\mu,n}\) simultaneously for all
\(a\in I\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\) gives
\(-B_Y\le\mu(a)=E_P[Y(a)]\le B_Y\).  Hence, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le\mu(a),                                                           \tag{20}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge\mu(a).                                                           \tag{21}
\]
In (20), both the raw lower expression and \(-B_Y\) are at most \(\mu(a)\);
in (21), both the raw upper expression and \(B_Y\) are at least
\(\mu(a)\).  Therefore the clipping rule preserves the inequalities, and
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\subseteq
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.              \tag{22}
\]
Taking probabilities in (22) and invoking the uniform event bound gives
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}
 \ge1-\alpha.                                                         \tag{23}
\]
Equations (19) and (23), together with joint measurability, verify every
condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\), so
\(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  Finally, (19) and monotonicity
of expectation imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le2B_Y.
\]
This proof uses no inverse-diameter or shrinking-width assertion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/3\). On this event, \(\max_x|p_x-\widehat p_x|\le[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\); moreover \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2)\le|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). Put \(e_{p,n}=[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\). If \(p=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) and \(p'=(p'_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), while \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) are fixed for every \(x\), then \[\sup_{a\in I}\left|\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|\le2|\mathcal X|\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n},\] and the right-hand side is \(o(r_n)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Under the relaxed outer marked sieve, feasibility gives \(|q_x/f_x|\le B_Y+b_{\mu,n}/2\), not \(|q_x/f_x|\le B_Y\). The original constant \(2B_Y|\mathcal X|\) is therefore false for feasible outer-sieve pairs. The corrected bound follows from the declared envelope and retains the same \(o(r_n)\) conclusion.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/3\). On this event, \(\max_x|p_x-\widehat p_x|\le[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\); moreover \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2)\le|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). Put \(e_{p,n}=[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\). If \(p=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) and \(p'=(p'_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), while \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) are fixed for every \(x\), then \[\sup_{a\in I}\left|\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|\le2|\mathcal X|\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n},\] and the right-hand side is \(o(r_n)\).
proposed.justification: The empirical cell masses are random inputs to the causal mixture and must enter the same simultaneous coverage event as the two transform channels.
proposed.gap: The blind-deconvolution comparators do not profile finite-stratum causal weights jointly with probability and marked transform restrictions.
proposed.consumer: The bound adds cell-count uncertainty to coverage and shows that its diameter contribution remains negligible relative to \(r_n\), while respecting the relaxed outer-sieve envelope.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected feasible-quotient bound introduces the declared outer-sieve families and \(b_{\mu,n}\), and its rate calculation directly uses the tuning and allowance definitions.
